ox.content.categories.accessories.faq_1_: For whey protein with 300 ml of water, 600 ml is enough. A mass gainer usually needs 800 ml or more, because the serving is larger. An 820 ml shaker suits both and leaves enough room to shake. The capacity is written into every product name.
Which shaker capacity should I choose?
ox.content.categories.accessories.faq_2_: Wash it straight after use instead of leaving it for hours. Most of the smell comes from milk or whey residue. If the smell stays, soak it overnight in warm water with a spoon of baking soda, then wash it. Leave it open until it dries.
How do I get rid of the protein smell in a shaker?
ox.content.categories.accessories.faq_3_: Yes. It goes into the same shipment as the supplements and arrives with them, and it adds no shipping charge. If your order is above {{threshold}} riyals, shipping is free for the whole order. You can also collect it with your order from the Al Khalidiyah branch in Madinah.
Does the shaker ship with the rest of the order?
ox.content.categories.accessories.intro: Accessories are the tools that make using supplements easier. The range starts with the shaker, and over time we add a travel pill case and a spare measuring scoop. A good shaker has a mixing ball that reduces clumping, does not leak, survives the dishwasher, and does not hold the smell of whey after washing. We state the capacity in millilitres in every shaker name, because a mass gainer needs more room than whey. Add it to the same order and it ships with it from Madinah at no extra shipping charge.
ox.content.categories.accessories.title: Shakers and Gym Accessories | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.faq_1_: BCAA is three branched chain amino acids: leucine, isoleucine and valine. EAA covers all nine essential amino acids, including those three. If your daily protein from food or whey is enough, you may not need either.
What is the difference between BCAA and EAA?
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.faq_2_: Glutamine is an amino acid abundant in muscle, and some people who train keep it in their routine after intense sessions. The common dose on labels is 5 grams, and it dissolves easily in water or with whey. It is not one of the basics for a beginner.
What does glutamine do for athletes?
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.faq_3_: Usually not. Whey protein already contains a good amount of branched chain amino acids, so if you are taking your protein serving you usually do not need a separate BCAA. It remains an extra option for anyone who prefers a light drink during a session.
Do I need BCAA if I drink whey protein?
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.intro: Amino acids are the building blocks protein is made of, and here they come as drinks or tablets. BCAA covers three branched chain acids; EAA covers all nine essential acids. You will also find glutamine, arginine and citrulline. If your food and your whey already cover your protein requirement, you may not need any of them. We say that plainly rather than let you buy everything.
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.title: BCAA and EAA Amino Acids | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_1_a: Yes. Casein is a common choice before bed because it digests and absorbs more slowly than whey. Whey is faster and suits the post training window better. Both count towards your daily protein requirement, so do not add an extra serving just because it is evening.
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_1_q: Can I drink protein before bed?
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_2_a: The source is the same, milk, and the main difference is absorption speed. Whey is faster, casein slower. That is why many people use whey after training and casein before bed. If you are buying only one, whey is usually the more flexible in use.
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_2_q: What is the difference between casein and whey?
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_3_a: Casein takes up more water than whey, so use about 250 to 300 ml of water or milk per scoop and shake it well. If you want it thicker, use less liquid until it is like a pudding.
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_3_q: How do I mix casein so it does not clump?
ox.content.categories.casein.intro: Casein is the milk protein that digests and absorbs more slowly than whey, which is why many people prefer it before bed or between meals that are far apart. Its texture is usually thicker than whey, and you can make it a thick shake or a pudding. One serving usually gives about 24 grams of protein. It is not a replacement for whey so much as an extra option for a different time of day.
ox.content.categories.casein.title: Casein Protein, Slow Release | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.collagen_beauty.fa: It is usually taken daily at 10 to 20 grams dissolved in water, coffee or any drink, hot or cold. It needs weeks of consistent use before judging any difference, and what you notice varies from person to person.
The difference is the source. Bovine is extracted from cattle hide, marine from fish skin and scales. Both are hydrolysed peptides that dissolve in drinks. Pick the source that suits you.
What is the difference between bovine and marine collagen?

Biotin is a B group vitamin that contributes to the maintenance of normal hair and skin. That is nutrition level wording, not a promise of a specific cosmetic result. The dose differs between products, so check the label before use.
ox.content.categories.collagen_beauty.in: Collagen peptides are a hydrolysed protein from a bovine or marine source, usually with no clear taste, dissolving easily in coffee and water. It is used daily, and any difference varies from person to person and takes time to judge. Here you will also find biotin and blends that combine more than one ingredient. We state the source and content of every product, and we do not promise you a result.
ox.content.categories.collagen_beauty.ti: Collagen Peptides, Marine and Bovine | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_1_a: The difference between the two times is small. What matters is sticking to a fixed daily dose, on training days and rest days alike. Some people prefer it after training with a meal.
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_1_q: When do I take creatine, before or after training?
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_2_a: The common dose for creatine monohydrate is 3 to 5 grams a day, but the scoop weight differs from one product to another. So check the scoop weight printed on the label. A loading phase is optional, not a requirement.
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_2_q: How many scoops of creatine a day?
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_3_a: Micronised is the same creatine monohydrate with finer particles, so it dissolves more easily. The active substance and the dose are the same. If plain monohydrate dissolves well for you, there is no need to change because of the name.
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_3_q: What is the difference between creatine monohydrate and micronised?
ox.content.categories.creatine.intro: Creatine monohydrate is among the simplest and most common forms of creatine. The body stores it in the muscles, and it contributes to energy production in short, high intensity efforts. The common dose on labels is 3 to 5 grams a day, on training days and rest days. We focus on monohydrate here because it is clear, simple and available in different grinds and at different prices.
ox.content.categories.creatine.title: Creatine Monohydrate in Saudi Arabia | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.daily_health.faq_1: After a long, sweaty session, on a hot day, or when travelling. On an ordinary day with a short workout, water is usually enough.
When do I use electrolyte tablets?
ox.content.categories.daily_health.faq_2: Look at three things on the pack: the number of strains, the colony forming units, and how it is stored. We write those numbers into every product description so you can compare easily.
How do I choose a probiotic?
ox.content.categories.daily_health.faq_3: Liquid chlorophyll is a green plant extract usually added to water and drunk as part of a daily routine. Some versions are flavoured and lighter in taste. We describe the product as the label does, with no promise of specific results.
What is liquid chlorophyll and how is it used?
ox.content.categories.daily_health.intro: Daily health covers the products that belong in your routine rather than at a training time: probiotics, electrolytes, concentrated greens and chlorophyll. You do not need all of them; pick the product that has a clear place in your routine. We state the key numbers and ingredients from the label so you can compare easily.
ox.content.categories.daily_health.title: Daily Health: Probiotics and Electrolytes | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.faq_1_: A mass gainer adds calories and protein to your day, so it can help you raise your total intake if reaching your calories from meals is hard. But its effect on your weight depends on your total food and training, not on the product alone.
Does a mass gainer add weight?
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.faq_2_: It depends on the product. Some packs count a serving as two scoops, some as more. The number is printed clearly on the label, and we repeat it in the product description. If the serving sits heavy, split it in two.
How many scoops of mass gainer a day?
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.faq_3_: Some mass gainers already contain creatine and some do not. Where it is present, check the amount before adding a separate creatine, so you know your daily total.
Does a mass gainer contain creatine?
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.intro: A mass gainer brings carbohydrates and protein together in one high calorie serving, for anyone who finds it hard to reach their daily calories from food alone. The serving is usually large compared with a whey scoop, so compare the calories and protein per serving instead of relying on the pack size alone. Make it an addition to your routine, not a replacement for meals.
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.title: Mass Gainer and Weight Gain Protein | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_1_a: With a meal that contains fat, at whatever time suits you. Many people take it with lunch or dinner. Consistency matters more than the exact hour.
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_2_a: EPA and DHA are the two active fatty acids in fish oil, and their number is one of the main things to compare when buying omega-3. Do not rely on the total fish oil on the front of the pack; look at the EPA and DHA per serving on the label.
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_2_q: What do EPA and DHA on the pack mean?
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_3_a: An omega-3 product on its own is fish oil concentrated on EPA and DHA, while a 3-6-9 blend brings three types of fatty acid into one capsule with less omega-3 in it. If you are buying for EPA and DHA, compare the amount printed per serving.
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_3_q: What is the difference between omega-3 and omega 3-6-9?
ox.content.categories.omega_3.intro: Omega-3 are fatty acids whose source in supplements is fish oil, and a common part of a daily routine. What matters when comparing products is the EPA and DHA per serving, not the total fish oil printed on the front. They are usually taken with a meal, and here you will find different fish oils and 3-6-9 blends.
ox.content.categories.omega_3.title: Omega-3 Fish Oil | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.plant_protein.faq_: Yes, when the amount is enough within your daily protein requirement. Blends that combine more than one source, such as pea and rice, give a fuller profile of essential amino acids.
Does plant protein contribute to building muscle?
Plant protein is free of milk by nature; gluten depends on the product. So check the label and the allergens on every pack before buying.
Is plant protein free of milk and gluten?

Because some plant sources, such as pea and rice, have a more noticeable taste and a thicker texture than whey. Many brands cover that with cocoa or vanilla, and you can try it with plant milk or in a smoothie instead of water alone.
Why does plant protein taste different?
ox.content.categories.plant_protein.intr: Plant protein is a protein powder from pea, rice or a blend of more than one source, for anyone who prefers a non animal source or avoids milk. A scoop usually gives about 20 to 24 grams of protein. Taste and texture vary between brands more than in some other protein categories, so the flavour you choose matters.
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.faq_1_: A pre-workout is usually taken about 20 to 30 minutes before training and, depending on the product, contains ingredients such as caffeine, citrulline and beta alanine. It is an optional extra, not a requirement for anyone.
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.faq_2_: Yes. There are stimulant free versions, and they suit anyone who trains at night or prefers to avoid caffeine. Look for "stimulant free" or "stim free" on the pack.
Is there a caffeine free pre-workout?
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.faq_3_: Light, temporary tingling with beta alanine is a common sensation for some people. If it bothers you, check the serving size or choose a product without it.
Why do I feel tingling after a pre-workout?
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.intro: A pre-workout is a supplement taken before training, and the formula differs from one product to the next. Some contain caffeine, some are stimulant free, and some lean on citrulline or beta alanine. What matters most is knowing the caffeine per serving and not combining more than one stimulant source without keeping count.
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.title: Pre-Workout Supplements | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_1_a: Concentrate is the simplest and most economical choice for many people. Isolate is higher in protein share and lower in lactose and fat. Casein absorbs more slowly, plant protein is for anyone who prefers a plant source, and a mass gainer puts protein, carbohydrates and calories into one serving.
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_1_q: What is the difference between the types of protein powder?
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_2_a: It depends on your daily protein need. A scoop usually gives about 20 to 25 grams; one scoop is enough for some people and others need more, depending on what they get from food. The number that matters is your total for the whole day.
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_2_q: How many scoops of protein a day?
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_3_a: Protein powder is a food supplement that completes your protein intake; it is not a replacement for food. Choose the type and amount by what you actually need, and read the label on every product. For medical conditions or medication questions, see your doctor.
ox.content.categories.protein.intro: Protein powder makes up for the protein your food lacks, and it is not one category. Here you will find whey concentrate for daily use, whey isolate for anyone who prefers a higher protein share and less lactose, casein for a different time of day, plant protein, and a mass gainer for anyone who needs more calories. Do not choose on the name alone. Compare protein per serving, number of servings, ingredients and price.
ox.content.categories.protein.title: Protein Powder in Saudi Arabia | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.faq_1_: In protein terms it can come close to a scoop of whey, but the calories and ingredients differ. The bar is practical away from home, while the scoop is usually more economical if you use it every day.
Is a protein bar a replacement for a scoop of whey?
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.faq_2_: Protein chips are made to give you more protein than ordinary chips; they are usually baked, and the protein source differs by product. Read the nutrition facts table instead of relying on the name.
What is the difference between protein chips and ordinary chips?
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.faq_3_: Because they are a simple snack that fits easily into your routine. Oats add carbohydrates and fibre, and peanut butter adds fat and calories. Each product has different ingredients, so read the label.
Why do we sell oats and peanut butter in a supplement store?
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.intro: Protein snacks are a practical choice between meals or when you are away from home. Here you will find protein bars, protein chips, oats and peanut butter. Compare protein, sugar and calories per serving or per piece, and pick the product that fits the way you eat instead of choosing on the name alone.
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.title: Protein Snacks and Protein Bars | OptimalX
It depends on the product and the dose printed on it. Vitamin D is fat soluble, which is why many people take it with a meal. If your product is a high dose, follow what the label says or see your doctor.
When do I take vitamin D?
Magnesium glycinate is one of the forms many people prefer in the evening because it is gentle on the stomach. But form and dose differ between products, so read the label.
Which form of magnesium suits the evening?
Yes, but check the label if you also take a multivitamin or another product, so the same elements are not repeated in doses you did not intend.
Can I take zinc with vitamin C?

Vitamins and minerals complete what your food may be missing, and they belong to the daily routine more than to a training time. Here you will find multivitamins, vitamin D3, vitamin C, zinc, magnesium and more. Do not stack many products at random. Compare the amount per serving, and make sure the same element is not repeated across products.
Vitamins and Minerals in Saudi Arabia | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.faq_1: Isolate goes through extra filtering, so its protein share is higher and its lactose and fat lower per serving. Concentrate is simpler and usually more economical. The difference that matters depends on your need, not on one costing more.
What is the difference between isolate and concentrate?
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.faq_2: ISO 100 is a product name from Dymatize, and it is a hydrolysed whey protein isolate. So it is a type of whey protein, not a separate category.
What is the difference between whey protein and ISO 100?
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.faq_3: Isolate usually contains less lactose than concentrate, which is why some people prefer it. But it is still derived from milk, so it is not the right choice for anyone avoiding milk completely.
Is isolate suitable for someone avoiding lactose?
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.intro: Whey isolate is whey protein that has gone through extra filtering, so the protein share per serving is higher and the lactose and fat lower. It suits anyone who watches protein and calories closely, or anyone who prefers less lactose. Some products here are hydrolysed, meaning broken in advance into smaller pieces. Compare products by your need, not by price alone.
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.title: Whey Protein Isolate, Authentic | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.faq_1: Both work, and the bigger difference is your total protein across the day. If you train on an empty stomach, before may suit you; if you ate a meal long enough before, after may suit you. There is no magic timing.
When do I take whey protein, before or after training?
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.faq_2: Whey itself is not high in calories. Its effect on your weight depends on your total intake across the day. You can use it in a calorie surplus phase or in a plan where you control calories, depending on how you prepare it and the rest of your food.
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.faq_3: It depends on the tub weight and the serving size. Bigger tubs give more servings, and the exact number is on the label under servings. We also put it in the product description so packs are easy to compare.
How many scoops are in a tub of whey protein?
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.intro: Whey protein is milk whey protein, and it is among the most used types of protein powder. It gives you a complete protein that fits easily into your routine, after training or between meals. When comparing, do not look at the tub size alone. Look at protein per serving, number of servings, flavour and ingredients.
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.title: Whey Protein in Saudi Arabia, Authentic | OptimalX
ox.content.faq.pdp_allergens_a: The allergens printed on the label appear in every product under the Note heading, for example milk, soy, wheat or nuts. If you have an allergy to a specific ingredient, check the product label before use.
ox.content.faq.pdp_storage_a: Keep the pack closed in a cool, dry place away from the sun, especially in summer.
ox.content.faq.pdp_storage_q: How do I store the product?
ox.content.faq.price_a: We choose products we know and can explain, and walk you through the servings, serving size, ingredients and how to use them, with free help if you need it.
ox.content.faq.price_q: How does OptimalX choose its products?
ox.content.glossary.bcaa.def: Three branched chain amino acids: leucine, isoleucine and valine.
ox.content.glossary.beta_alanine.def: An amino acid in some pre-workouts; it can cause a light, temporary tingling.
ox.content.glossary.biotin.def: A B group vitamin that contributes to the maintenance of normal hair and skin.
ox.content.glossary.casein.def: The milk protein that absorbs more slowly than whey; many people take it before bed or between meals.
ox.content.glossary.citrulline.def: A common ingredient in pre-workouts, used in formulas made for training.
ox.content.glossary.closing: Could not find the term you were looking for? Send it to us and we will add it with an explanation.
ox.content.glossary.collagen.def: Hydrolysed collagen peptides, usually dissolved in a drink and taken as the product directs.
ox.content.glossary.concentrate.def: Whey with basic filtration, usually less expensive than isolate.
ox.content.glossary.creatine.def: A compound the body stores in muscle; it contributes to energy production in short, high intensity effort.
ox.content.glossary.eaa.def: The nine essential amino acids the body does not make.
ox.content.glossary.electrolytes.def: Minerals and salts such as sodium, potassium and magnesium, found in some hydration drinks and tablets.
ox.content.glossary.glutamine.def: An amino acid abundant in the body and in muscle; it appears in some post-workout products.
ox.content.glossary.hydrolysed.def: Protein whose chains have been cut into smaller pieces beforehand.
ox.content.glossary.isolate.def: Whey protein with extra filtration; it usually has more protein and less lactose and fat.
ox.content.glossary.iu.def: A unit used to measure some vitamins, such as vitamin D3.
ox.content.glossary.lactose.def: The milk sugar, usually lower in isolate than in concentrate.
ox.content.glossary.loading.def: An optional phase in which some people start with a higher creatine dose for a short time.
ox.content.glossary.magnesium.def: A mineral that comes in several forms; people choose the form by their need and preference.
ox.content.glossary.mass_gainer.def: A powder that brings protein and carbohydrates together in a high calorie serving.
ox.content.glossary.micronised.def: Creatine monohydrate with finer particles so it dissolves more easily.
ox.content.glossary.nutrition_facts.def: The table that lists calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat and other nutrients per serving.
ox.content.glossary.omega_3.def: Fatty acids found in fish oil supplements; many people compare products by their EPA and DHA content.
ox.content.glossary.page_title: Supplement Glossary: Whey, Isolate, Creatine | OptimalX
ox.content.glossary.plant_protein.def: Protein from plant sources such as pea, rice or a plant blend.
ox.content.glossary.pre_workout.def: A supplement taken before training; the formula differs by product and may include caffeine, citrulline and beta alanine.
ox.content.glossary.probiotic.def: Products that contain strains of live bacteria; they differ in the number of strains and the amount of bacteria in each.
ox.content.glossary.scoop.def: The scoop inside the pack; its weight differs between products.
ox.content.glossary.serving.def: The amount the label sets for one use.
ox.content.glossary.stim_free.def: A pre-workout without stimulants such as caffeine.
ox.content.glossary.vitamin_d3.def: A fat soluble vitamin that comes in different doses depending on the product.
ox.content.glossary.whey.def: A protein extracted from milk whey and one of the most widely used protein powders.
ox.content.glossary.zma.def: A blend of zinc, magnesium and vitamin B6. The exact formula differs between products.
ox.content.goals.energy.faq_1_a: Usually 20 to 30 minutes before training. If you take caffeine from coffee or anything else the same day, count it in your total. At night, watch what caffeine does to your sleep.
ox.content.goals.energy.faq_2_a: Yes. There are stimulant free versions, and they suit anyone who trains in the evening or prefers to avoid caffeine. Look for "stimulant free" or "stim free" on the pack.
ox.content.goals.energy.faq_2_q: Is there a caffeine free pre-workout?
ox.content.goals.energy.faq_3_a: It varies by product. The number on the pack is the reference, and we put it on the product page so you know the caffeine content before you buy. If you are sensitive to it, start with a smaller serving, following the product instructions.
ox.content.goals.energy.faq_3_q: How much caffeine is in one serving?
ox.content.goals.energy.intro: If your goal is to walk into training with energy and focus, here you will find pre-workouts with and without caffeine, plus electrolytes and some amino acids. Choose by when you train and how much caffeine suits you, and do not stack more than one source of stimulants without counting it.
ox.content.goals.energy.need_1_line: Pre-workout with or without caffeine, taken before training as the product instructions say.
ox.content.goals.energy.need_1_title: Energy and focus before the session
ox.content.goals.energy.need_2_line: Stimulant free versions for evening training, or for anyone who prefers to avoid caffeine.
ox.content.goals.energy.need_3_line: Electrolytes added to water on hot days or after prolonged sweating.
ox.content.goals.energy.need_help: Not sure what suits you? Send your question and we will help.
ox.content.goals.energy.title: Pre-Workout Energy and Focus Supplements | OptimalX
ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_1_a: Not necessarily. A multivitamin completes your routine; it does not make up for a varied diet. If you use more than one product, check the labels so you do not repeat the same nutrients unnecessarily.
ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_1_q: Do I need a multivitamin if my diet is balanced?
ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_2_a: It depends on the dose printed on the product. Many people take it with a meal, because vitamin D is fat soluble. If the product is a high dose, follow the pack instructions or your health provider's guidance.
ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_2_q: When do I take vitamin D3?
ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_3_a: Yes, and many people take them with a meal. But check each product's dose and make sure you are not repeating the same nutrients from more than one source.
ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_3_q: Can I take omega-3 and vitamin D at the same time?
ox.content.goals.general_health.intro: General health supplements are what goes into your daily routine rather than around a training time: a multivitamin, vitamin D3, omega-3, magnesium, zinc and a probiotic. You are not meant to take all of them. Pick what has a clear role for you, and check the labels before combining more than one product.
ox.content.goals.general_health.need_1_l: Multivitamins for men or for women, with options such as vitamin D3 and magnesium.
ox.content.goals.general_health.need_2_l: Omega-3 with a clear EPA and DHA content, taken with a meal.
ox.content.goals.general_health.need_3_l: Probiotics, electrolytes and daily routine options, as you need them.
ox.content.goals.general_health.need_3_t: The rest of the daily routine
ox.content.goals.general_health.need_hel: Unsure what you need, or about combining two products? Ask us.

ox.content.goals.hair_skin.faq_1_a: As the product instructions say, usually dissolved in water, coffee or any drink. It takes weeks of consistent use, and what you notice varies from person to person.
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.faq_1_q: How do I use collagen peptides?
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.faq_2_a: Biotin contributes to the maintenance of normal hair and skin, but that is not a promise of a specific cosmetic result. Check the product's dose on the label.
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.faq_3_a: The difference is the source. Bovine comes from cattle, marine from fish. The choice comes down to your preference and the product's source.
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.faq_3_q: What is the difference between bovine and marine collagen?
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.intro: Hair, skin and nail supplements are products taken as part of your daily routine, such as collagen, biotin, zinc and omega-3. We present them as part of nutrition, not as a promise of a result. Consistency matters more than chasing high doses or stacking many products.
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.need_1_line: Bovine or marine collagen peptides, easy to add to coffee or water.
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.need_2_line: Options such as zinc and vitamin C within your daily routine.
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.need_3_line: Omega-3 with a suitable meal, and a clear EPA and DHA content.
ox.content.goals.hair_skin.need_help: Not sure which product suits your routine? Ask us.

ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.faq_1_a: A mass gainer adds calories and protein to your day, so it can be a practical option when reaching your calories from food is hard. Its effect on your weight depends on your total food and training.
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.faq_1_q: Does a mass gainer add weight?
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.faq_2_a: Isolate usually gives a higher protein share and less lactose and fat than concentrate. If calories or lactose are your focus, it may suit you better. If you have no specific reason, concentrate is usually enough.
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.faq_2_q: What is the difference between isolate and concentrate during a cutting phase?
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.faq_3_a: No. The creatine is the same in both phases; what differs is your diet and your training, not the type of creatine.
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.faq_3_q: Is there a creatine made for cutting?
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.group_gain: For anyone training and raising their calories steadily who needs an easier way to add protein and calories.
A mass gainer brings protein, carbohydrates and calories together in one serving.
Calories and protein in one serving
Whey protein with milk or oats to raise protein and calories as you need.

ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.group_lean: For anyone watching their calories who wants protein without many calories from the product itself.
Whey isolate, with a higher protein share and less lactose and fat per serving.
Protein bars and protein chips as a practical snack between meals.

ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.h1: Ideal Weight Supplements: Mass and Cutting
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.intro: Ideal weight is a goal with two directions, and it differs from person to person. If you are raising your calories, you may need a practical way to add protein and calories. If you are watching calories, you may prefer more protein and fewer calories. A supplement does not set your goal for you, but it helps you close a clear gap in your routine.
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.need_help: Your goal needs more than a product page. Send your question or book a consultation, and we will help you understand the options.
ox.content.goals.ideal_weight.title: Ideal Weight Supplements: Mass and Cutting | OptimalX
ox.content.goals.performance.explainer_1: Gym supplements are the products you use to complete your routine around training. Four are the most common: protein to complete your daily requirement, creatine to support short high intensity work, pre-workout for energy and focus depending on its formula, and amino acids as an optional extra. You are not meant to use all of them.
ox.content.goals.performance.explainer_2: For a beginner, the base is regular training, sleep and enough food. After that, look at the actual gap you have. If protein from food falls short, whey can be a practical option. If your training is regular, creatine is a well known option. Pre-workout and amino acids are extras, not a condition for starting.
ox.content.goals.performance.explainer_t: What are gym supplements, and what does a beginner need?
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_1_a: Whey protein if your food does not cover your protein requirement, and creatine monohydrate as a simple option within your training routine. Pre-workout and amino acids are later additions, not a condition for starting. The base is still sleep, food and sticking to training.
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_1_q: Which supplements go with the performance goal?
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_2_a: No. Many products overlap in what they do, and some are just an optional extra. Whey protein already contains amino acids, for example, so you usually do not need a separate BCAA just because you use whey.
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_2_q: Do I need all of these supplements together?
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_3_a: Protein completes your daily protein requirement, while creatine works differently and supports energy production in short high intensity work. Both can be part of the same routine.
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_3_q: What is the difference between creatine and protein?
ox.content.goals.performance.intro: If your goal is to progress in training and build a structured supplement routine, start with the basics: protein to complete your daily requirement, creatine as a practical option for regular training, and pre-workout and the other extras depending on what you actually need. You do not need everything from day one.
ox.content.goals.performance.need_1_line: Whey concentrate or isolate to complete your protein requirement.
ox.content.goals.performance.need_2_line: Creatine monohydrate at a fixed daily dose, as the product instructions say.
ox.content.goals.performance.need_3_line: Pre-workout with caffeine or stimulant free, depending on when you train.
ox.content.goals.performance.need_3_titl: Energy and focus before the session
ox.content.goals.performance.need_help: Starting from zero? Ask us what you need first, and we will lay out the options without complication.
ox.content.goals.performance.title: Gym Performance Supplements | OptimalX
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_1_a: One scoop usually gives 20 to 25 grams of protein, but what you actually need depends on your whole day. If your meal after training covers your requirement, you do not need a scoop just for the timing.
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_1_q: How many scoops of protein after training?
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_2_a: Yes. Casein is a common choice before bed because it absorbs more slowly than whey, and both count towards your daily protein requirement.
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_2_q: Can I drink protein before bed?
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_3_a: Magnesium is a mineral involved in normal body and muscle function, and many people who train take it in the evening. The form and the dose vary by product, so check the label.
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_3_q: What does magnesium do for someone who trains?
ox.content.goals.recovery.intro: Recovery supplements are what comes after training and before sleep, and the base is still food, rest and sleep. They help you complete that routine when you have a clear gap: whey protein is the fast option, casein the slower one, and you also find magnesium and electrolytes as you need them.
ox.content.goals.recovery.need_1_line: Whey protein after training or between meals to complete your protein requirement.
ox.content.goals.recovery.need_2_line: Casein as the slow option before bed, or across long gaps between meals.
ox.content.goals.recovery.need_3_line: Magnesium and electrolytes, depending on your routine, how much you sweat and when you take them.
ox.content.goals.recovery.need_help: Want to sort out your post-training routine? Send us your question and we will help.
ox.content.goals.recovery.title: Recovery Supplements After Training and Before Sleep | OptimalX

ox.content.thankyou.intro: Three steps before the first serving.
ox.content.thankyou.line_accessories: Wash the shaker straight after use, and leave the lid open so it dries.
ox.content.thankyou.line_amino_acids: As the label says: a drink or tablets, following the directions printed on it.
ox.content.thankyou.line_casein: A scoop with the amount of liquid the label gives. A thick texture is normal.
ox.content.thankyou.line_collagen_beauty: Add it to coffee or water as the product directs, and stick with it before you judge it.
ox.content.thankyou.line_creatine: Use it daily at the dose printed on the product, on training days and rest days.
ox.content.thankyou.line_daily_health: As the label says. Electrolytes when you need them, probiotics as the product directs.
ox.content.thankyou.line_digital_library: The download link is in your account and in your email now.
ox.content.thankyou.line_mass_gainer: Take the serving the label gives. If it is too much for you, split it however suits you.
ox.content.thankyou.line_pre_workout: Start with the serving printed on the pack, and mind the caffeine, especially at night.
ox.content.thankyou.line_services: The confirmation or the answer reaches you by email.
ox.content.thankyou.line_snacks_bars: Keep them somewhere cool, and use them as a snack in your day.
ox.content.thankyou.line_vitamins: As the label says, and check the ingredients of your other products so you do not double up on the same element.
ox.content.thankyou.line_whey_protein: Mix it with water or milk, as you prefer and as the product directs, and shake it well.
ox.content.thankyou.step_1: Read the label once, all of it: serving size, number of servings, ingredients and expiry.
ox.content.thankyou.step_2: If the product is new to you, stick to the printed serving and do not mix several products at random.
ox.content.thankyou.step_3: Set a routine and stick to it. Consistency matters more than chasing the perfect timing.
ox.content.thankyou.storage: Keep the pack closed in a cool, dry place away from the sun, especially in summer.
ox.content.thankyou.title: How to start using your product
